title: Lenders who call borrowing 'efficiency' turn a discount sale of the borrower's future labor into an appearance of prudent service
body:
- Lenders marketed credit cards and consumer loans as tools for "efficiency" and "smoothing consumption."
- The framing obscured that consumers were selling their future earning capacity at unfavorable rates.
- The capital-efficiency argument applies only to debt used to acquire cash-flowing assets, not depreciating goods or current consumption.
conversion: Calling borrowing 'efficiency' or 'smoothing' turns a discount sale of the borrower's future labor into an appearance of prudent financial service.
